summary: Fourteen days of high-quality CGM data show strong overall glucose outcomes, with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL and 86.0% time in range. The principal safety concern is 5.1% time below range, including repeated readings in the low 40s and recurring low exposure from late evening through early overnight. Daytime rises, especially from 14:00 to 17:00 local time, frequently occur with no recorded carbohydrates and are managed through UAM, SMB, temporary basal, corrections, and Dynamic ISF. This can produce substantial IOB followed by delayed declines. The evidence supports reviewing a single continuous overnight target change from 90 to 100 mg/dL while keeping basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and automation settings unchanged until meal and insulin delivery are better separated.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage and cadence support time-of-day analysis. The authoritative profile is complete and declared applicable to the period. Treatment and loop telemetry are extensive but condensed.
analysis_steps.evidence: There are 3,995 valid CGM entries, 98.7% coverage, no invalid or duplicate entries, a five-minute estimated cadence, ten gaps, and a largest gap of 65 minutes. The profile contains all basal, target, CR, ISF, and DIA values, and profile_context reports historical_applicability as yes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Meal, CR, correction, and absorption conclusions depend on meal-linked carbohydrate and insulin records. Basal conclusions require relatively fasting-like intervals.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate, e-carb, activity, or low-treatment entries are present. Representative telemetry does not reconstruct every insulin delivery around each excursion.

analysis_steps.findings: Recurrent hypoglycaemia is the dominant safety constraint despite strong overall time in range. Low exposure clusters overnight and in the early evening, while the greatest high-glucose burden occurs during the afternoon.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose is 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0%, time above range 8.9%, time below range 5.1%, SD 39.7 mg/dL, and CV 32.6%. Local-time TBR is 11.4% at 00:00, 18.5% at 01:00, 10.1% at 02:00, 10.2% at 03:00, and 15.3% at 19:00. Severe-low clusters reached 42 mg/dL on August 13, 41 mg/dL on August 14, and 42 mg/dL on August 21.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Any target, basal, ISF, Dynamic ISF, or SMB review must prioritize reducing low exposure and avoid strengthening insulin delivery in response to afternoon highs alone.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Symptoms, confirmatory measurements, activity, carbohydrate treatment of lows, and complete preceding insulin delivery are unavailable.

analysis_steps.findings: The recurring 23:00 to 03:00 low pattern supports reviewing the continuous overnight target rather than assuming a basal defect. Daytime rises are too confounded by meals and automation to justify more basal. Evening lows may reflect accumulated correction insulin as well as basal and target exposure.
analysis_steps.evidence: The profile target is 90 mg/dL from 23:00 through 08:00, coinciding with substantial late-evening and overnight TBR. Local means are 93.3 mg/dL at 00:00 and 90.6 mg/dL at 01:00. The 06:00 to 08:00 period is comparatively stable, while afternoon highs are followed by increasing low exposure around 18:00 to 19:00.
analysis_steps.dependencies: The overnight target should be evaluated before changing overnight basal. Basal interpretation also depends on residual IOB, SMB, corrections, temporary targets, and activity.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No labelled fasting tests or complete insulin timelines isolate individual basal segments.

analysis_steps.findings: No CR segment has a meal-linked test. Static ISF cannot be separated from Dynamic ISF, SMB, temporary basal, and other IOB. The prolonged declines in several response windows support retaining awareness of long insulin action, but they do not independently validate or invalidate the 10-hour DIA.
analysis_steps.evidence: No carbohydrate treatments were recorded. Variable sensitivity spans approximately 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U versus the static ISF of 56 mg/dL/U. Several correction-labelled windows continued falling for four to six hours, including 234 to 56 mg/dL after two hours and 61 mg/dL after six hours on August 14.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR assessment depends on known carbohydrate amount, meal time, and bolus time. ISF and DIA assessment depends on separating manual correction, SMB, temporary basal, Dynamic ISF, food, and activity.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: There are no clean meal tests, isolated correction tests, or complete IOB decay observations.

analysis_steps.findings: UAM and SMB are heavily involved because observed loop records repeatedly show COB 0 during glucose rises. They appear to compensate for unrecorded or unannounced meal effects, but the data do not isolate SMB as the cause of later lows. Activation and delivery settings therefore remain unchanged.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM are enabled, SMB is always enabled, and no carbohydrates are recorded. Representative loops show microbolusing during rises and IOB values of 4.73 U and 5.935 U during high glucose. Daytime highs are sometimes followed by marked declines or hypoglycaemia.
analysis_steps.dependencies: SMB and UAM changes should follow evaluation of the overnight target and reconstruction of insulin delivery around lows. Meal announcement strategy must be assessed before reducing automation used to handle COB-0 rises.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The package does not provide complete consecutive SMB sequences, activation reasons, or meal-linked comparisons.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF can make effective sensitivity substantially stronger during high glucose and may combine with UAM, SMB, and temporary basal to accumulate IOB. However, it is also designed to reduce dosing near lower glucose, and causality is not isolated. Absolute max basal and max IOB settings are high relative to observed profile basal, but neither limit was reached or proven causal.
analysis_steps.evidence: Dynamic ISF is enabled at 70%, while Autosens is disabled. Variable sensitivity reached 37.9 mg/dL/U at BG 262 mg/dL and 27.8 mg/dL/U at BG 245.7 mg/dL. The configured limits are 12 U/h and 25 U, while representative IOB peaked near 5.9 U and an effective maxSafeBasal near 4 U/h appeared in loop reasoning.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Dynamic ISF, SMB limits, static ISF, basal, and target should not be changed together. Safety-limit changes require individualized pump and insulin-context verification.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No isolated comparison shows glucose response with and without Dynamic ISF, and the condensed data do not establish individualized safe maximum insulin limits.

analysis_steps.findings: There is no user-declared meal strategy in analysis_context and no observed carbohydrate entry from which to infer prebolus timing or immediate bolus percentage. The COB-0/UAM-led pattern may conceal meal timing or CR problems. More aggressive upfront insulin is unsupported because high IOB and delayed lows are already present.
analysis_steps.evidence: The declared meal_strategies array is empty, strategy_stable_for_period is null, and Nightscout contains zero carbohydrate entries. Recurring daytime rises are managed with correction-labelled boluses and temporary basal. Multiple response windows continue falling for four to six hours.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Numeric prebolus or immediate bolus recommendations require a documented meal with carbohydrate amount, bolus timing, glucose response, and total automated insulin.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage, meal carbohydrate amount, meal composition, and meal-linked bolus execution are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb strategy or duration can be inferred. Carbohydrate absorption settings are largely untested because observed COB remains zero. Delayed rises and rebounds cannot be attributed to meal absorption without meal-linked evidence.
analysis_steps.evidence: There are zero carb entries, zero e-carb entries, no e-carb duration, and no carb-linked six-hour response. Current absorption settings are 8 mg/dL/5 min minimum carb impact and seven hours maximum absorption.
analysis_steps.dependencies: E-carb assessment requires a reproducible delayed meal rise after separating meal timing, IOB, SMB, temporary targets, corrections, and low treatments.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked carbohydrate amount, e-carb start offset, e-carb duration, or absorption curve is available.

analysis_steps.findings: The most defensible first review is a single continuous overnight target change from 90 to 100 mg/dL across the 23:00 and 00:00 target rows. This directly addresses recurring overnight low exposure without asserting an unproven basal, CR, ISF, DIA, or automation defect. All other settings should remain unchanged while the target response and complete insulin context are observed.
analysis_steps.evidence: The low pattern recurs across 23:00 to 03:00 with TBR of 10.1% to 18.5%, and the current target is 90 mg/dL throughout that interval. Afternoon highs are confounded by COB-0 UAM responses, while severe lows and delayed declines argue against strengthening insulin settings.
analysis_steps.dependencies: The overnight target rows represent one continuous 23:00 to 08:00 window and should be reviewed as one change. Automation review follows only after observing that change. Meal strategy follows after collecting one structured six-hour meal record.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Residual IOB, activity, low treatment, and detailed insulin delivery still limit attribution of overnight lows to the target alone.

strengths: CGM data quality is good, with 98.7% coverage and no invalid or duplicate readings.
Overall time in range is strong at 86.0%, with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL.
Glucose is comparatively stable from approximately 06:00 to 08:00 local time.
The authoritative AAPS profile is complete and declared applicable to the review period.
The 10-hour DIA preserves awareness of prolonged insulin activity during a period containing delayed declines.
issues: Time below range is 5.1%, with repeated severe readings in the low 40s and concentrated low exposure overnight and around 18:00 to 19:00 local time.
Recurring afternoon highs are followed in some cases by substantial insulin accumulation and delayed declines, so stronger basal, CR, or ISF settings could increase hypoglycaemia risk.
No meal strategy is declared and no carbohydrate or e-carb treatments are recorded, preventing separation of meal timing, CR, UAM, SMB, and absorption effects.
Dynamic ISF produces a wide range of effective sensitivity, but its independent contribution cannot be separated from SMB, temporary basal, corrections, and existing IOB.
The configured max basal and max IOB limits provide broad ceilings, but this package does not establish individualized replacement values or show that either ceiling caused the observed lows.

recommendations.title: Review one continuous overnight target change first
recommendations.description: The recurring 23:00 to 03:00 low pattern supports reviewing the overnight target before changing basal or automation. The two target rows form one continuous overnight window.

suggested_change.scope: Change the 23:00 and 00:00 target rows together as one continuous overnight-target adjustment, after independent verification.

recommendations.title: Hold automation settings while evaluating the target
recommendations.description: Keep SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, SMB limits, max basal, and max IOB unchanged during the first observation period so the effect of the overnight target can be distinguished.

suggested_change.candidate_value: No automation change during the initial overnight-target review
suggested_change.scope: Reconstruct IOB, SMB, temporary basal, corrections, temporary targets, and activity around any continuing lows before considering an automation change.

recommendations.title: Capture one structured recurring meal
recommendations.description: A single six-hour meal record would better separate meal timing and CR from UAM, Dynamic ISF, correction stacking, and delayed absorption.

suggested_change.current_value: No declared or observed meal strategy
suggested_change.candidate_value: Record carbohydrate amount, meal time, bolus time, any prebolus or immediate percentage, CGM response, and total manual and automated insulin for six hours
suggested_change.scope: Use the observation before assigning numeric prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, CR, or e-carb values.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Review changing the continuous 23:00 to 08:00 target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL, represented by both the 23:00 and 00:00 target rows.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight TBR repeatedly reaches 10.1% to 18.5%, with means near 90 to 105 mg/dL and severe lows elsewhere in the period. A higher overnight target is a more conservative first profile adjustment than reducing basal without fasting evidence or altering automation while residual IOB remains unresolved.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After independent verification and one-at-a-time implementation, compare at least three to seven representative nights for 23:00 to 07:00 TBR, glucose direction, IOB, SMB, temporary basal, corrections, temporary targets, activity, and low treatment.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight lows are supported, but residual evening IOB, SMB, corrections, activity, and the 90 mg/dL target remain competing causes. Review the overnight target first and retain this basal until fasting-like evidence separates those dependencies.
Local 05:00 TBR is 4.8%, but no fasting test isolates this one-hour segment. Uncertainty from residual IOB and the overnight target supports withholding a basal change.

The 06:00 to 08:00 period is comparatively stable, with means near 100 to 111 mg/dL and low TBR. One isolated 42 mg/dL event and missing insulin and activity context do not support changing this segment.

Daytime glucose rises are observed, but zero carbohydrate records and COB-0 UAM responses make meals, bolus timing, and automation more plausible than proven basal deficiency. Meal-linked evidence is required before changing this segment.

Local 16:00 has the highest mean and TAR, but it is followed by increasing low exposure. Accumulated SMB, temporary basal, corrections, and Dynamic ISF are unresolved dependencies, so increasing basal would carry additional low risk.

Evening TBR and severe lows are concerning, but preceding afternoon correction insulin and missing activity and low-treatment data prevent attribution to this basal segment. Evaluate the target and complete insulin context first.
Later low exposure could involve this segment, but preceding high-glucose correction and residual IOB remain major uncertainties. No fasting-like evidence supports a concrete replacement value.
No carbohydrate amount or meal-linked bolus response is available for this segment. Overnight lows cannot be assigned to CR because meal execution, correction insulin, and IOB are unknown.
There are no documented meals or carbohydrate amounts in this window. The relatively stable early-morning glucose pattern and missing meal evidence do not support a CR change.
Morning and afternoon rises could reflect unrecorded meals, prebolus timing, or UAM response. Without carb amount and bolus timing, these rises do not prove that this CR is weak.

Evening lows occur after daytime highs and substantial automated or correction insulin, but no meal bolus is identifiable. CR, SMB, Dynamic ISF, and IOB cannot be separated, so a concrete change is unsupported.
No meal-linked carbohydrate or bolus record exists for this period. Overnight low exposure is more directly addressed by reviewing the target while retaining CR pending structured meal evidence.

Correction-labelled windows show large and variable responses, but Dynamic ISF, SMB, temporary basal, food, activity, and pre-existing IOB are unresolved. The static ISF cannot be isolated, and changing it with the target would confound safety evaluation.

Local TBR is 11.4% at 00:00, 18.5% at 01:00, 10.1% at 02:00, and 10.2% at 03:00. Residual IOB remains uncertain, but raising the continuous overnight target is a more conservative first review than changing basal, ISF, or automation.
This daytime target already matches the candidate overnight target. Daytime highs are confounded by unrecorded meals and automation, while later lows argue against lowering the target.

Local 23:00 TBR is 10.1% and the low pattern continues after midnight. This row and the 00:00 row form one continuous overnight target, so they must remain aligned when evaluating a single overnight-target adjustment.

Several correction-labelled responses continue for four to six hours, supporting continued IOB awareness. The data lack a clean insulin decay test and do not support shortening or lengthening DIA while Dynamic ISF and repeated automated insulin remain active.

SMB and UAM respond to recurring COB-0 rises and may also contribute to cumulative IOB, but complete SMB sequences and meal records are absent. Altering them with the overnight target would confound attribution and could worsen daytime highs.

Broad SMB availability is relevant to COB-0 rises, but no activation-condition comparison or announced-meal execution is available. The current group is internally interpretable, and changing it before target and meal verification is unsupported.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: High IOB and delayed lows make cumulative delivery important, but representative records do not show the full number and spacing of SMBs. Interval and minute limits should not be changed together or alongside the overnight target without delivery reconstruction.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: The ceilings are broad relative to profile basal, but neither was reached or shown to cause the observed lows, and other effective safety constraints limited representative delivery. Individualized replacement values cannot be derived from this package, so independent review is appropriate without an invented change.

Dynamic ISF sometimes produces much stronger effective sensitivity during highs, but it also varies with glucose conditions and cannot be isolated from UAM, SMB, temporary basal, or corrections. Change is withheld until the target response and insulin delivery around lows are evaluated.

Zero carbohydrate and e-carb entries mean the absorption model has no meal-linked response for evaluation. COB-0 UAM behavior, rather than entered-carbohydrate absorption, dominates the observed telemetry.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Do not assign a numeric prebolus or immediate bolus percentage from this package. Keep SMB/UAM unchanged while one recurring meal is documented, and do not introduce e-carbs unless a reproducible delayed rise is demonstrated after separating IOB, SMB, temporary targets, corrections, and low treatments.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: No meal strategy is declared, no carbohydrates are recorded, and daytime rises are handled as COB-0 UAM events. More aggressive upfront insulin could add to substantial IOB and delayed hypoglycaemia, while reducing UAM without a reliable announced-meal strategy could worsen the daytime rises.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Capture one recurring meal with carbohydrate amount, meal timestamp, bolus timestamp, any actual prebolus and immediate bolus percentage, CGM trajectory, temporary targets, and all manual and automated insulin for six hours.

exceptions.pattern: An elevated glucose level with substantial IOB or a trend already turning downward
exceptions.suggestion: Do not interpret the preceding peak alone as evidence for a stronger CR, longer prebolus, or larger immediate bolus fraction.
exceptions.rationale: Several high-glucose episodes were followed by large declines over two to six hours while Dynamic ISF, SMB, temporary basal, and corrections could all remain active.

exceptions.pattern: A documented recurring meal that is initially stable and then rises several hours later without correction stacking
exceptions.suggestion: Review regular carbohydrate entry versus e-carb representation only after the delayed pattern is reproduced; no amount, start offset, or duration is currently supported.
exceptions.rationale: Current telemetry has no carb-linked absorption curve and cannot distinguish delayed absorption from omitted entry, rebound treatment, or automation effects.

implementation_steps: Independently confirm that the authoritative profile values and local-time interpretation match the active AAPS configuration before considering any change.
Review the 23:00 and 00:00 target rows as one continuous overnight window; if the candidate is accepted, change only that overnight target from 90 to 100 mg/dL.

Monitor glucose closely and compare at least three to seven representative nights, including TBR, glucose direction, IOB, SMB, temporary basal, corrections, temporary targets, activity, and low treatment.
Keep basal, CR, ISF, DIA, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, SMB limits, max basal, and max IOB unchanged during that observation period.
If significant lows continue, reconstruct the full insulin timeline around them before considering a separate basal or automation review.
After the overnight assessment, record one representative recurring meal for six hours before considering numeric prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, CR, or e-carb changes.
Discuss the severe-low pattern and any proposed configuration change with the diabetes care team, making changes one at a time.
education: A low target can encourage more insulin delivery or less insulin suspension, but residual IOB may still be the main cause of an individual low.
UAM responds to glucose rises when carbohydrates are not represented as COB; it is not automatic duplicate counting of entered carbohydrates.
Dynamic ISF can make effective sensitivity stronger or weaker than the static ISF, so a correction-labelled bolus is not an isolated ISF test when automation remains active.
Afternoon hyperglycaemia followed by an evening low can reflect delayed cumulative insulin rather than insufficient afternoon basal.
E-carbs represent anticipated extended carbohydrate absorption and are not the same as a pump extended bolus.
Time-of-day averages identify recurring risk windows but do not by themselves prove which profile or automation parameter caused the pattern.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and does not provide medical advice.
Every proposed change must be independently verified, made one at a time, and followed with close glucose monitoring.
Repeated readings in the low 40s are a material safety concern and warrant prompt review with the diabetes care team.
Unexpected lows, impaired awareness, suspected pump or sensor failure, or inability to keep glucose safe require use of the established urgent-care and hypoglycaemia plan.
No AAPS setting should be changed automatically from this analysis.
